claim: beta=40 cliff at n=130 is structural, not a 250-bit MPFR precision artifact
hypothesis_tested: Paper §6.3 reports abrupt SD-BKZ disadvantage at n=130 β=40 (-1.334 nats, 0% win, d=-9.70 at 250-bit MPFR). Reviewer concern: could the cliff be a numerical precision artifact in the squared-form GSO recurrence at 250-bit MPFR?
interpretation: Doubling MPFR precision (250→500 bit) softens the mean SD-BKZ disadvantage by +0.088 nats (6.4% of baseline magnitude) but does not change the sign of the disadvantage in any of 20 seeds. Win rate remains 0%. Cohen's d vs zero is actually STRONGER at 500-bit (-11.4 vs -9.70) because variance tightens with precision. The small Welch t=+2.39 captures a measurable-but-negligible numerical shift; the phenomenon itself is not precision-driven.

paper_impact.section_7_4_limitations_add: The β=40 cliff at n=130 was tested for precision-sensitivity by re-running 20 seeds at 500-bit MPFR (double the 250-bit baseline). Mean advantage moved from -1.370 to -1.282 nats (Δ=+0.088 nats); win rate stayed at 0/20. The cliff is therefore structural, not a numerical artifact of the squared-form GSO recurrence at 250-bit.
